key_insight: dLI-RADS achieved 80% lesion-level accuracy versus 74% for LI-RADS in internal evaluation, meeting the study’s non-inferiority criterion.
clinical_relevance: The method could support CT-based assessment of small liver lesions using interpretable imaging features, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Analyzes manually segmented liver lesions on multiphase CT.
Combines neural network predictions with quantitative measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features.
Uses logistic regression to estimate hepatocellular carcinoma probability.
evidence_signal: This multicenter retrospective study excluded lesions larger than 40 mm and used 10,000-repetition bootstrap testing with a 5% non-inferiority margin; internal accuracy met non-inferiority (p = 0.04), while external results are not reported in the supplied excerpt.
watch_item: Manual lesion segmentation adds workflow burden, and prospective clinical performance remains to be established.
paper_title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
